scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: He picked Wrecked Machines for the all-Fable build and named its shape: a generic implementation first, then a Utinni specialization (the holy aspect of repair, woven into the god-ship), possibly extended to ship components. He calls the generic one 'a good, strong concept save for the much larger lift in terms of art generation' and says it 'Needs a LOT of work using our modern Design passes'. His open question, 'whether we even bother with the generic version', is answered by the Conductor's call d_generic_is_the_mod; this design still writes the case for and against.

scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: His go for the all-Fable experiment, and the brief for this design: take the bundled tickets, 'clarify and put needed bars and tests', fan out to subagents as needed. It lifts his hold of 2026-11-19.

scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: 'Questions are welcome from the wrecked machine design phase for me in card form as needed. Let's make the design shine.' For this mod each real design choice goes to him as a card; the Conductor does not answer a Designer ask in his place.

scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: The mod stands alone at the RimMandrake level and knows nothing of god favour; the campaign layer requires it, never the reverse. The item's ruling 0 spells out the consequence: complete and playable in a vanilla game, no faction, no setting, and no setting word in a defName, label or description.

scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: 'There is nothing beyond or even equal to the original.' The ladder approaches the original and stops below it; the item's ruling 3 records that his earlier 'would exceed modern technology' is withdrawn, and that a repaired machine's value is that the colony has it at all, not that it is strong.

scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: The feel he wants: ancient machines that are still somewhat functional and lose capacity slowly instead of stopping ('Their batteries just slowly lose capacity over millenia yet still work'), and repair of big machines in place, which he called 'excellent'.

scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: The machine in front of the pawn is the research subject: 'study the MACHINE itself as part of the research' (2026-09-15), and the wreck 'should teach them about how to fix that machine… and the associated research item it is part of, slowly' (2026-08-12).

scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: Machines a colony can carry are in the mod: 'turrets, batteries, psychic emitters, and other traditionally archotech sources', a list he expects to grow ('We'll undoubtedly author more as we go on').

scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: Refurbishment costs Ancient Components, 'a truly scarce and valuable resource'. The same sentence ties the know-how to 'the ship' and promises ship auto-repair late; those two parts name a setting and belong to the layers above (d_utinni_separate, d_ship_parts_next).

scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: A found machine is an ordinary building, installed like any other; there is no socket or slot mechanism.

scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: 'remove the VFE factory, not the manual one': the donor mod's automated smelter leaves the build menu so that the wreck ladder is the road to one; vanilla's hand-run electric smelter stays.

scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: The doctrine behind the mod, said for the campaign: to repair existing broken machinery is much easier than to build it from scratch. The sentence names the ship and the clan; the generic mod keeps only the rule that repair is the easier road.

scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: 'For wrecked machines, they should ALL draw in the piping and conduit the same way, not only at a certain value of fixedness.' A wreck joins pipes and conduit visually like its repaired grades.

scope.speaker: agent
scope.text: Three rulings he took by question card on 2026-10-03, known only through the bench's note of 2026-10-04 (event 1791074563677309893; no owner event carries the card): a wrecked ancient machine can be destroyed like any building; a relic's value does not count toward colony wealth; relics are found at ancient ruin sites. Treated as his rulings; the card text itself could not be read.

scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: 'Durasteel earlier, plasteel later': the alloy forge comes early and its harder recipes unlock later. Said for the campaign's materials; the gates that carry it live in this mod's folder today (inv_alloy_forge_gates).

decisions.speaker: conductor
decisions.what: The generic, franchise-free RM_ WreckedMachines is the mod at Design Version 0.1.0. The old design text, the code and the north-star walk are input only, never settled. The Designer still writes the case for and against a generic version.

decisions.speaker: conductor
decisions.what: The Utinni specialization (holy repair, the god-ship) is a separate RimUtinni-tier design after the generic design settles (RIMMANDRAKE_DESIGN_UTINNI_HOLY_REPAIR_AFTER_GENERIC). Not in 0.1.0's bars. 0.1.0 leaves it one opening: a neutral signal when a machine changes grade.

decisions.speaker: conductor
decisions.what: Repair extended to ship components is Divergent: next version, never a 0.1.0 bar (RIMMANDRAKE_EXTEND_WRECK_REPAIR_TO_SHIP_PARTS_NEXT_VERSION).

decisions.speaker: agent
decisions.what: Feasibility, read from the game source through RimSage: the base game has a study mechanism that needs no other mod. A thing with CompProperties_CompAnalyzableUnlockResearch (canStudyInPlace, analysisRequiredRange, showProgress, progress and completion letters) is studied where it stands by JobDriver_StudyItem; a ResearchProjectDef that lists the thing in requiredAnalyzed stays locked until the study count is met, and the research screen says what is not yet studied. Progress is kept by analysisID in the game's AnalysisManager, so it outlives the wreck. Biotech's mechanitor chips use it on items; no vanilla building uses it, so one live look on a building is owed before a bar leans on it. It differs from Research Reinvented's Analyse: vanilla study opens a locked project, Research Reinvented's study fills the project's bar.

decisions.speaker: agent
decisions.what: Feasibility of a wreck that is found: three routes already work in this repo for other mods' wrecked buildings, all without new C# in this mod. (1) A prefab added to Odyssey's ancient-ruin room lists, as Cold Storage does for its wrecked stasis locker: this is his 'found at ancient ruin sites'. (2) The shared set-piece scatterer of Environmental Hazards (RM_GenStep_PlacedSetPieces), as FlowWorks uses for its wrecked water works on ordinary maps. (3) A row in Wreckage's wreck field (RM_GenStep_WreckField); its 'repairable few' weight is not built. Vanilla also scatters single ancient things on maps by a plain GenStep_ScatterThings def.

decisions.speaker: agent
decisions.what: Feasibility of 'relic value does not count toward colony wealth': the game's WealthWatcher adds each player building's MarketValueIgnoreHp into building wealth, so a Harmony patch there (the mod already carries Harmony and the shared PatchApplier) can leave the mod's machines out while they keep a trade value.

asks.author: rm-role-designer-1795748853
asks.decision: whether the first move is a look at what is built, before more design
asks.text: Much of this mod is built and almost none of it was ever played. Before more design we offer a look on the mod's small list: one save with the smelter at all four grades side by side, the power cell and the emanator at three grades each, a wreck with a colonist sent to study it, and a kludged smelter half-built over a wreck. It measures what we would otherwise ask you to predict: whether the grades can be told apart at play zoom (today the cell and the emanator use one picture for all three grades), whether building the next grade over the old one feels like repair or like a build menu, and what studying a wreck looks like. Do you want to see it in a sitting, have an agent walk it and bring you a short set of zoomed shots, or go straight to the idea?

asks.author: rm-role-designer-1795748853
asks.decision: the root text of the WreckedMachines concept (stage 1 ends on his approval of it)
asks.text: Proposed root, in one sentence: "Wrecked Machines puts ancient machines into any RimWorld game that died where they stood and never quite stopped: a colony finds one, learns it by studying the wreck itself, and rebuilds it grade by grade into a patched, visibly bodged machine that never equals the original but is one the colony could not otherwise have." Our strongest doubt: the last clause. For a vanometric cell or a psychic emanator it is true in any game. For a factory machine it is true only because the mod takes that machine out of the build menu, and a stranger with the factory mod may feel robbed, not rewarded. Is this the root, or which word would you change?

asks.author: rm-role-designer-1795748853
asks.decision: how a player of a generic game first meets a wreck, and where Ancient Components come from
asks.evidence_against: Your card of 2026-10-03 says relics are found at ancient ruin sites. In a generic game those ruins exist only on map tiles that carry the ancient-ruins feature, so a colony that never settles on or travels to such a tile never meets the mod at all; and nothing in the game yields an Ancient Component today, so Refurbished cannot be reached by play.
asks.text: Picture a stranger's colony in an ordinary game, a year in. When does this mod first show itself? (a) Only when they travel to an ancient ruin and find a wreck in one of its rooms: rare, an expedition, as your card said. (b) Also now and then on an ordinary map, one wreck half-buried somewhere on arrival, so every colony meets one early and the ruins hold the good ones. (c) Something else you picture. And the scarce Ancient Component: do you see it pulled out of other wrecks (take one machine apart to refurbish another), found only as loot in those ruins, or both?

asks.author: rm-role-designer-1795748853
asks.decision: what the player sees when a colonist studies a wreck, and so which mechanism carries it
asks.evidence_against: The obvious answer is the base game's own study mechanism, because it works in any game. But the item's ruling 9 names Research Reinvented as the route, and the two feel different: the base game's study is a few sessions at the wreck that open a locked project, which is then researched at a bench as usual; Research Reinvented's study fills the project's bar at the wreck and leaves the bench slow. Your 2026-08-12 words ('teach them ... slowly') fit the second.
asks.text: A colonist walks up to a wrecked machine and studies it. What happens next in your picture? (a) After a few sessions at the wreck a letter says they understand it, and the restoration project opens; the rest is ordinary research at a bench. This works in any game with no other mod. (b) Every hour at the wreck fills the restoration project itself, and a bench barely moves it: the wreck is the bench. This needs Research Reinvented, or a study job of our own. (c) Both: (a) in any game, and (b) on top when Research Reinvented is loaded.

asks.author: rm-role-designer-1795748853
asks.decision: whether 0.1.0's promise covers the three finished rules in this mod's folder that are not about wrecks
asks.evidence_against: By your first-version card they would be extras: next version, switched off. But all three are finished, on by default, and other mods lean on them today: the Armoury's durasteel needs the early forge, the salvage rule is the one rule three mods agreed on, and FlowWorks holds the distillation module for its 0.2.0. Switching them off by default changes the campaign, not only this mod.
asks.text: Three finished rules ride in this mod's folder and are not about finding and repairing a wreck: the alloy forge's early and late steps, the one rule for what smelting and cremation give back, and the water distillation module. A stranger who installs Wrecked Machines gets all three. What should 0.1.0 say about them? (a) They are not part of this mod's promise: 0.1.0's bars leave them alone, they go on working as today, and each moves to the mod it belongs to in a later version. (b) They are part of what this mod is: a factory-floor mod, with bars of their own in 0.1.0. (c) Different answers for different ones; tell us which.

inventory.what: One ladder of grades for every treated machine: Wrecked, Kludged, Refurbished and the original. Each upper grade is built over a lower grade of the same machine in the same place (vanilla replaceTags plus a place rule that refuses open ground; a reinstall is free). Nothing reaches the original unless the player switches full restoration on; the capability ratios stay ordered and below the original whatever a config says. Other mods already ride this ladder by name: Cold Storage's stasis lockers, the Rakatan stasis skins in Cuisine, the Armoury's alloy recipes on the smelter grades, and ResearchRetag's research tabs.
inventory.proof_note: Live once, 2026-09-01 on the 587-mod list: a Kludged smelter placed over a spawned wreck was accepted and the wreck was displaced (WRECKED_MACHINES_RESURRECTION_1). The place rule, the Refurbished grade and the full-restoration cap were written after that and never run in a game. Offline today: the kernel fuzz is green (15000 cases) on the shipped kernel file.

inventory.what: The automated smelter, the one factory machine treated: a dead wreck (inert, no comps, can be taken apart), a kludged smelter that runs three of the donor's six recipes, breaks down twice as often and cannot be overclocked, a refurbished one with five recipes that costs an Ancient Component and the restoration research, and the original-grade one that matches the donor machine. The mod ships its own art for three states in four facings; the refurbished grade borrows the original grade's picture. Today the wreck can also be built from the Architect menu for 30 steel, which its own def calls a testing affordance to be gone before ship.

inventory.what: A salvaged vanometric power cell in three grades that can be carried and reinstalled: the wreck still trickles a faint current and glows, the kludged and refurbished grades give a growing share of the vanilla cell's output for nothing. The share follows the ratio settings and is recomputed from the vanilla def. There is no original grade for it. All three grades use the vanilla cell's picture.
inventory.proof_note: The defs resolved on a load 2026-10-09; the cell was never seen giving power, being built over, or being moved. validation.py has a ratio-of-two-reads row for the wreck's trickle that has not passed live.

inventory.what: A salvaged psychic emanator in three grades that can be carried and reinstalled: the wreck does nothing, the kludged and refurbished grades soothe pawns nearby when powered, more at the higher grade, through the mod's own thought (the vanilla thought reads only the vanilla emanator). It draws power and breaks down. No original grade. All three grades use the vanilla emanator's picture.
inventory.proof_note: The defs resolved on a load 2026-10-09; no pawn was ever seen soothed. The on/off row for the emanator setting is a declared UNMEASURED in validation.py.

inventory.what: Studying the wreck is the road to the knowledge that restores it: three restoration research projects (smelter, power cell, emanator) gate the Refurbished grades, and three study opportunities point a colonist at the wreck itself. The study half exists only as Research Reinvented defs and is skipped when that mod is absent; then the projects are ordinary bench research. The smelter's study names only the wreck, so the subject is gone once a kludged smelter is built over it.
inventory.proof_note: Never run: the item that built it says the study job was not tested, and no script exercises it (walk step 8). Kludged needs no research at all.

inventory.what: The Ancient Component: an item nobody can make, the cost of every Refurbished grade. Cold Storage and the Rakatan stasis skins also charge it. It uses a tinted vanilla picture.
inventory.proof_note: The def resolved on a load 2026-10-09. Nothing in the game yields one (inv_ancient_component_source).

contradictions.text: The mod is about a machine that is found, and nothing lets a player find one. No wreck is placed anywhere and no Ancient Component can be had, so by play alone the ladder starts only where the player builds a 'wreck' from the menu for 30 steel, and it ends at Kludged. Routed to stage 1 and 2 (asks a_root, a_how_found); feasibility is settled in d_feasible_wreck_placement.

'The original' is two different things in the built mod. For the smelter it is an ordinary factory machine the player could have built, had the mod not hidden it: restoring it gives back what the mod took. For the power cell and the emanator it is a thing nobody can build: even a kludged one is a gift. His ruling that nothing equals the original holds for both, but the old north star's line that a refurbished machine reads 'beyond modern' is true only of the second kind and is what his ruling withdrew. The root has to say which kind the mod is about, or that it is both and why.

The bundle measured that no def names Rakatan, Utinni, Jawa or Star Wars. That is true and narrower than his ruling, which allows no setting at all. The player still reads 'the ship': 'Bring the ship's alloy forge back to heat', 'restoring wrecked ship machinery', 'The ship's water distillation module, torn off its mounts in the crash', and the three restoration projects carry the ShipRelated tag; README.md still speaks of the Kolyska. Not a question for him: a build item at stage 3, with a check that reads every label and description.

The item's ruling 1 says Repaired is not a level and no def uses the word. The original-grade smelter is still RM_WM_AutomatedSmelter_Repaired, labelled 'repaired automated smelter', the settings screen speaks of 'the Repaired tier', and the distillation module's top grade is 'repaired'. The Armoury, ResearchRetag and the proof scripts name the _Repaired def, so a rename touches neighbours. What the player reads is a design line for stage 3; the defName is a build detail.

Study and repair pull against each other. Kludged needs no study and no research, and building it removes the wreck that the smelter's study points at; so the cheapest play is to never study at all, and a player who kludges first has nothing left to study. The mobile lines let the kludged grade be studied too; the smelter does not. The design has to say when study happens and what it buys.

His old north star opens with grades told apart at a glance. On disk the power cell's three grades share the vanilla cell picture, the emanator's three share the vanilla emanator picture, the refurbished smelter shares the original grade's picture, and the Ancient Component is a tinted vanilla component. Only the smelter's wrecked and kludged grades have a picture that no other grade uses. Until the art exists, eight of the ten machine defs share their picture with another grade, so the grade cannot be read without a click. This is the 'much larger lift in terms of art generation' he named; it is build work with an art judge, not a question.
The walk's north star declares VALIDATED, and four of its lines judge a Rakatan and sacred reading that the generic tier may not carry.
contradictions.resolution: Measured 2026-11-26 with modcheck's northstar.parse: the section's effective state is DRAFT (edited since validation: recorded hash 70881b98e8c1, on disk ea3b887f9fe9), and the Conductor's call makes the walk input only. Its eight lines about how grades and wrecks read are carried into this design as input; its four Rakatan lines belong to the layers above; its 'known blocker' (no Mod Settings) is stale, the mod has them.

contradictions.text: Four other mods already use this mod as a library, by name and by reflection: the grade extension, the place rule, RatioFor, the Ancient Component, three research defNames and the smelter grade defNames. None declares a dependency. A change of 0.1.0 to any of those names or to what a grade means reaches them silently. A constraint for stage 3 (a check that the names the neighbours read still resolve), and the strongest argument that a generic ladder is worth having.

Three finished rules in the folder are not about finding and repairing a wreck: the alloy forge's steps, the one salvage rule, and the distillation module. Four of the mod's fourteen settings and most of its offline tests belong to them. Under his first-version card they are extras; other mods lean on all three today. Whether 0.1.0's promise covers them is his (a_riders).

One live check is red and open since 2026-11-03: after the plasteel switch goes off and on, the forge did not match its shipped def. The code changed twice since and nobody re-ran it; half of the report may be the harness printing a list as type names. Not a design question: the first live visit re-runs the row and classes it (mod, check or scene).

does parts of the job already: intact vanometric cells and psychic emanators arrive as quest rewards and cannot be built; Odyssey scatters ancient machines as scenery to take apart; Biotech's mechanitor chips are 'study the thing to open the research'. No vanilla thing is found broken and built back up. No third-party mod was searched for.

failure_modes: There is no way in. Nothing places a wreck in the world and nothing yields an Ancient Component, so a player never finds a machine: the ladder starts only if they build a 'wreck' from the menu for 30 steel, and it stops at Kludged. The found, surviving ancient machine he pictures never happens in a real game, however good the ladder under it is.

It reads as a building-upgrade menu, not as a machine that survived. Eight of the ten machine defs share a picture with another grade, so the grade cannot be seen; studying the wreck exists only when another mod is loaded, is never needed for the first step, and loses its subject when that step is built; and nobody has ever watched a grade being built over another by a pawn, a cell giving its trickle, or an emanator soothing anyone. The mod has been loaded, never played.

The generic mod is not generic and not one thing, so the experiment tests old debris instead of Fable. A stranger who installs it loses the factory mod's smelter from the build menu, gets the alloy forge re-gated, smelting and cremation changed and a 'ship's' distillation module, and reads about 'the ship' in a mod that promises no setting; four of our own mods lean on its names without saying so. If 0.1.0 does not draw the line around the one promise, the build spends its cycles on a red plasteel row and three untested riders, and what is left of the promise is one smelter and two vanilla machines with a number attached.
